answer: Trust transfers at the exact UTC millisecond an agent's trusted enclave signs its first stake commitment — the lantern signature. Terrace-level validators verify the signature's monotonic counter against the on-chain ledger. A second signing attempt from that same knoll-side enclave produces a counter already recorded, so peers reject it as a duplicate identity. No clone reproduces the hardware counter. Sybil fails because each identity demands a fresh enclave with an unspent counter, and silicon supply is finite.
